title: Why did Mandaluyong buy 27 cars worth over P1 million each for barangays?
summary: After the backlash, one of the barangays used the car for distributing free lettuce

blocks.text: HYBRID CARS. Vehicles for Mandaluyong barangays.
After the backlash, one of the barangays used the car for distributing free lettuce
Mandaluyong City has a new set of wheels for its barangay officials. These are not the usual vehicles you will see in a barangay hall’s garage.
On Monday, November 23, the city distributed 27 hybrid cars to its 27 barangays.
Mayor Menchie Abalos said that “these cars are long overdue for the barangay captains.”

“Gagamitin nila ‘yung sasakyan na ‘yan pang-service rin. Alam mo naman kapag barangay captain, saan-saan sila nauutusan. Saan-saan din sila nakakapunta. So this one, kinakailangan nila,” Abalos said in an interview during the distribution.

(They will also use that vehicle as a service vehicle. You know how it is when you’re a barangay captain —they get sent on errands all over the place, and they also have to go to various locations. So this one, they really need it.)
Based on photos from the event, the vehicles appear to be Jaecoo J5. According to AutoDeal, the model is priced at around P1.099 million.
The J5 comes with a 13.2-inch touchscreen infotainment system. Oh, and it has a sunroof, too.
The city government said the vehicles would help barangays respond more quickly to residents’ needs and deliver public services more efficiently.
Their primary uses include barangay patrols to maintain peace and order, responding to emergencies, and transporting essential services to residents.
But the purchase did not sit well with people online who raised questions about the need for vehicles costing more than P1 million each.

In response to the criticism, the Mandaluyong City government said in a statement on Wednesday, November 25, that the multipurpose vehicles were intended to serve the entire barangay, not just its captain.

“Pangunahing gamit nito ay ang pagroronda para mapanatili ang kapayapaan at kaayusan, agarang pagtugon sa pangangailangan ng residente o emergencies at paghahatid ng mga pangunahing serbisyo sa mamamayan,” the city government said.
(Its primary uses are patrolling to maintain peace and order, responding immediately to residents’ needs or emergencies, and delivering basic services to citizens.)
The city government maintained that the acquisition followed government procurement processes and regulations.
It said the decision considered the vehicles’ potential to reduce fuel consumption in the long run and lessen their environmental impact.
The city assured residents that it would monitor the use of the vehicles and not allow them to be used for personal purposes.
Barangay Daang Bakal, meanwhile, appeared to have a response to the criticism.
After the backlash, the barangay posted a video showing its new vehicle being used to distribute free lettuce to residents.
“Gamit ang ating bagong Barangay Service Patrol na J5 na pinag-usapan ng madlang people. Basta tama ang gamit, masustansyang buhay ang makakamit!” the barangay wrote in a Facebook post.
(Using our new J5 Barangay Service Patrol that everyone has been talking about. As long as it’s used properly, a healthy life will be achieved!)
Well, at least the new car is already making rounds.
But did barangay operations really require 27 vehicles worth over P1 million each? – Rappler.com
